context.analysis:
## Overview
This hybrid architecture gradually modernizes a legacy insurance claims platform over three years. It decouples the new cloud-based user experience from the on-premises mainframe system of record.

## Key Elements
* Policyholders and Brokers (External Users)
* Claims Adjusters (Internal Users)
* Modern Claims Platform (Azure App Service / Azure SQL, West Europe)
* Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Service Bus and Azure API Management)
* Legacy Mainframe (On-premises COBOL/DB2 System of Record)
* Identity Provider (Azure Active Directory / Entra ID)

## Relationships
* Users to Modern Claims Platform: HTTPS (REST/GraphQL) with OIDC/OAuth2 authentication via Azure AD
* Modern Claims Platform to Legacy Mainframe: mTLS (TLS 1.3) over secure hybrid connection via Anti-Corruption Layer
* Modern Claims Platform to Azure Key Vault: Managed Identities for secure credential retrieval

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Platform: Azure App Service and Azure SQL for managed hosting and minimal operational overhead
* Integration & Messaging: Azure Service Bus with dead-letter queues and Azure API Management for the Strangler Fig pattern and 1-day rollbacks
* Security & Auth: Azure AD (Entra ID) with MFA, OAuth2/JWT tokens, and Azure Key Vault for certificate management
* Infrastructure: Terraform or Bicep for Infrastructure as Code across the hybrid environment

## Rationale
The managed Azure services offset the team's low cloud experience while accelerating delivery of high-performance adjuster screens. The Anti-Corruption Layer and API Management insulate the fragile, change-constrained mainframe from cloud updates and guarantee zero data loss.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims platform with a modern hybrid cloud solution while maintaining business continuity. It provides online claim submission and adjuster workspaces while supporting the step-by-step migration of claim types.

## Key Elements
- Policyholders and Brokers (Users)
- Claims Adjusters (Users)
- Customer Portal (React SPA / Azure Container Apps)
- Adjuster Workspace (Node.js/Java / Azure Container Apps)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACA Integration Service)
- Migration Analytics Container (Node.js/Python / Azure Container Apps)
- Azure Service Bus (Event Broker)
- On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of Record)
- Azure Active Directory (Identity Provider via OIDC/OAuth2)

## Relationships
- Policyholders interact with Customer Portal via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- Adjusters interact with Adjuster Workspace via HTTPS
- Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace publish/subscribe to Azure Service Bus via AMQP
- Anti-Corruption Layer integrates Azure Service Bus with On-Premises Mainframe via mutual TLS (mTLS) over Azure ExpressRoute
- All services authenticate against Azure Active Directory via OIDC/OAuth2 and Azure Managed Identities

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps (ACA): Chosen to host microservices given the team's limited cloud experience by abstracting Kubernetes complexity
- React SPA & Azure Static Web Apps: Delivers a responsive, modern frontend for customer claim submissions
- Azure Service Bus: Ensures asynchronous, guaranteed event delivery and prevents claim loss (R-04)
- Azure ExpressRoute & mTLS: Secures hybrid connectivity between Azure and the on-premise mainframe
- Node.js/Java & Python: Power the backend microservices and migration analytics container

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture decouples modern web interfaces from the legacy mainframe using an Anti-Corruption Layer and asynchronous messaging, ensuring zero claim loss. Furthermore, Azure Container Apps and blue-green deployments enable rapid 1-day rollbacks per claim type while working within the team's cloud skill level.

Customer Portal.analysis:
## Overview
- Modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform by gradually replacing a 30-year-old mainframe while ensuring zero lost claims.
- Combines an on-premises COBOL/DB2 mainframe with cloud-native Azure services to deliver modern digital claim processing.

## Key Elements
- Policyholders and Brokers (Users)
- Claims Adjusters (Users)
- Customer Portal (React SPA / Azure Container Apps)
- Adjuster Workspace (Node.js/Java / Azure Container Apps)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACA Integration Service)
- Azure Service Bus (Azure Service Bus)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2 on-prem)
- Azure Active Directory (Identity Provider)

## Relationships
- Policyholders and Brokers -> Customer Portal: Submits online claims [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Customer Portal -> Azure API Gateway: Routes requests and submits data [HTTPS]
- Customer Portal -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes and subscribes to events [AMQP]
- Customer Portal -> Azure Active Directory: Authenticates users [OIDC/OAuth2 with PKCE]
- Customer Portal Components: Claims UI, Auth Manager, API Client, and State & Storage Components interact internally [Local Storage API / TypeScript]

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript: Powers the Customer Portal frontend for high responsiveness and maintainability.
- Azure Container Apps: Hosts containers with managed scaling to accommodate low cloud team experience.
- Azure Service Bus: Enables reliable asynchronous messaging to prevent lost claims during migration.
- Azure Active Directory: Centralizes single sign-on security via OIDC and OAuth2.
- Bicep/Terraform: Automates infrastructure provisioning to enforce immutable deployments.

## Rationale
- The hybrid architecture abstracts expensive mainframe changes through an anti-corruption layer while migrating claim types individually within a 3-year timeline.
- Managed cloud services on Azure reduce operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience while satisfying strict performance and security constraints.

Adjuster Workspace.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system with a modern cloud platform while maintaining hybrid operations. The Adjuster Workspace provides a web application enabling claims adjusters to process and manage claims efficiently.

## Key Elements
- Adjuster Workspace (Node.js/Express BFF, React Presentation Component)
- Azure Cache for Redis (Local Cache / Read Model Repository)
- Azure Service Bus (Command Dispatcher and Event Broker)
- Azure Active Directory / Identity Provider
- Legacy Mainframe / Anti-Corruption Layer (External System)
- Azure Monitor / OpenTelemetry

## Relationships
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Workspace: Interacts with and manages claims via [HTTPS]
- BFF Layer -> Azure Cache for Redis: Serves cached read models via [TCP/TLS]
- BFF Layer -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes asynchronous write commands via [AMQP]
- Adjuster Workspace -> Azure Active Directory: Authenticates users via [OIDC/OAuth2]
- BFF Layer -> Legacy Mainframe (via ACL): Synchronizes claims data via [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps: Runs containerized BFF and UI services to minimize cloud operational overhead.
- Node.js/Express: Powers the Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) layer for token handling and API orchestration.
- React: Renders dynamic claim forms and UI components.
- Azure Cache for Redis: Provides low-latency caching to meet sub-2s load requirements.
- Azure Service Bus: Handles asynchronous messaging and event-driven data distribution via [AMQP].
- OpenTelemetry & Azure Monitor: Ensures distributed tracing, circuit breaking, and sync-lag alerting.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed Azure services to accommodate a team with limited cloud experience while ensuring sub-2-second load times via Redis caching. It decouples the adjuster interface from slow mainframe responses, fulfilling strict performance, security, and hybrid migration constraints.

Anti-Corruption Layer.analysis:
## Overview
The system is an Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system. It enables online claim submission and adjuster workflows in Azure while maintaining the legacy mainframe as the system of record.

## Key Elements
- Policyholders and Brokers: External users submitting claims online
- Claims Adjusters: Internal users managing claims in the web application
- Customer Portal: React SPA hosted in Azure Container Apps
- Adjuster Workspace: Node.js/Java application hosted in Azure Container Apps
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACA Integration Service): Middleware container isolating the mainframe
- Internal Components: Routing Mediator, Domain Translator, Outbox Processor, DLQ Management, Telemetry Publisher
- Azure Service Bus: Messaging broker using AMQP
- On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Legacy system of record accessed via CICS Transaction Gateway

## Relationships
- Customer Portal -> Anti-Corruption Layer: Submits online claims [HTTPS/REST]
- Adjuster Workspace -> Anti-Corruption Layer: Manages claims [HTTPS/REST]
- Anti-Corruption Layer -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes and consumes events [AMQP]
- Routing Mediator -> Domain Translator: Forwards requests [gRPC]
- Domain Translator -> On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Translates and sends requests [Mutual TLS over Azure ExpressRoute / CICS Transaction Gateway]
- DLQ Management Component -> Azure Service Bus: Processes poisoned messages [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps: Container hosting for cloud components chosen for managed simplicity given limited cloud experience
- Spring Cloud Gateway / .NET Yarp: Routing Mediator implementation for dynamic traffic steering and circuit breaking
- Apache Camel / custom mapping engine: Domain Translator for JSON to COBOL copybook mapping
- Azure Service Bus: Reliable messaging backbone enforcing transactional outbox and DLQ patterns
- Azure Key Vault: Secure credential storage for isolated service accounts
- OpenTelemetry & Azure Monitor: Centralized hybrid observability and business metric telemetry

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture safely decouples modern Azure cloud applications from the fragile legacy mainframe using an Anti-Corruption Layer. It guarantees business continuity, transactional consistency (R-04), and a rapid 1-day fallback per claim type (R-06) while respecting strict mainframe batch windows and cost constraints.

Migration Analytics Container.analysis:
## Overview
This hybrid cloud architecture modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform by migrating claim types from a 30-year-old mainframe to Azure while maintaining strict data consistency. A dedicated Migration Analytics Container provides executive visibility, automated reconciliation, and discrepancy triage to de-risk the 3-year migration.

## Key Elements
- Claims Operations Director and Migration Program Manager (Users)
- Migration Analytics Container (Azure Container Apps)
- Reconciliation Engine Component (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Metrics Aggregator Component (Python/Pandas)
- Discrepancy Triage Service Component (Node.js)
- Analytics API & UI Component (Express/React)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) and Azure Service Bus

## Relationships
- Migration Analytics Container to Anti-Corruption Layer via gRPC over mTLS
- Reconciliation Engine to Azure Service Bus via AMQP for event consumption
- Analytics API to Management Clients via HTTPS/REST
- Reconciliation Engine to legacy DB2 via Anti-Corruption Layer for data comparison

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps: Container hosting chosen for simplicity
- Node.js/TypeScript & Python/Pandas: Component runtimes for reconciliation and telemetry
- Azure Database for PostgreSQL: State store with AES-256 encryption at rest
- KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling): Scales analytics workloads to respect the 23:00-05:00 batch window
- Azure Managed Identities & Azure RBAC: Zero-trust authentication and authorization

## Rationale
The architecture isolates legacy interactions behind an Anti-Corruption Layer and enforces automated reconciliation to guarantee zero data loss. Utilizing managed Azure services minimizes operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience.

Azure Service Bus.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old on-premises COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a cloud-native Azure platform. It processes insurance claims via a hybrid architecture while maintaining the mainframe as the system of record.

## Key Elements
- Policyholders and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Customer Portal (React SPA / Azure Container Apps)
- Adjuster Workspace (Node.js/Java / Azure Container Apps)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACA Integration Service)
- Azure Service Bus (Premium Tier)
- On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe

## Relationships
- Customer Portal -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes claim submission events [AMQP 1.0]
- Adjuster Workspace -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes and subscribes to claim processing events [AMQP 1.0]
- Anti-Corruption Layer -> Azure Service Bus: Integrates asynchronous messaging events [AMQP 1.0]
- Azure Service Bus -> On-Premises Mainframe: Relays sync queues via private hybrid connectivity [AMQP 1.0 / ExpressRoute]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Service Bus Premium: Required for VNet integration, Private Link, and Service Bus Sessions
- AMQP 1.0: Protocol for secure, cross-platform multiplexed messaging
- Terraform / Bicep: Infrastructure as Code for repeatable deployments and drift prevention
- Microsoft Entra ID: Authentication mechanism replacing SAS connection strings with Managed Identities and Azure RBAC Data Actions

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes behind an Anti-Corruption Layer while safely migrating claim types one by one. Azure Service Bus guarantees zero claim loss, FIFO processing order, and rapid rollback capabilities within the existing operational constraints.
